The '''S-thread booster''' was technology that could be used to create new [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperspace routes]] and also keep such routes open. It was extremely expensive to use and could be deployed either in [[Realspace/Legends|realspace]] or in [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]], with the latter type of the device being known as the [[non-mass S-thread booster]]. [[Simu-tunnel/Legends|S-thread]] boosters were utilized to maintain the [[Koros Trunk Line/Legends|Koros Trunk Line]] route linking the [[Empress Teta system/Legends|Empress Teta system]] and the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] as well as the [[Gandeal-Fondor Hyperlane]] between the worlds [[Gandeal]] and [[Fondor/Legends|Fondor]]. The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] also used non-mass S-thread boosters in the creation and maintenance of the [[Sanctuary Pipeline/Legends|Sanctuary Pipeline]] and [[Byss Run/Legends|Byss Run]] hyperlanes.

==Description==
The S-thread booster was a piece of technology that could be deployed in [[Realspace/Legends|realspace]]&mdash;or, in the case of [[non-mass S-thread booster]]s, in [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]&mdash;in order to brute-force open a new hyperspace tunnel and then keep the newly created [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] open. [[Simu-tunnel/Legends|S-thread]] boosters were extremely expensive to use; nevertheless, they were sometimes utilized to complement more conventional hyperspace [[Star map/Legends|charting]] methods and were frequently used when creating secret military routes.<ref name="TEA" />

==History==
[[File:KorosTrunkLineGHW-TEA.jpg|thumb|right|300px|S-thread boosters were used to keep the Koros Trunk Line hyperlane open.]]
Over the [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]] following the [[Colonist/Legends|settlement]] of the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core's]] [[Empress Teta system/Legends|Koros system]] around [[27,500 BBY]] and culminating shortly before the [[Galactic Constitution Conference|founding]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]<ref name="TEA" /> in [[25,053 BBY]],<ref name="TORE">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref> hyperspace [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] charted the route known as the [[Koros Trunk Line/Legends|Koros Trunk Line]], which was facilitated through the use of S-thread boosters and connected the Koros [[Star system/Legends|system]] to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], the Republic's [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Galactic Core]]. During the construction of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|''Executor''-class Star Dreadnought]] [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']] at the [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]] [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyard]] planet [[Fondor/Legends|Fondor]], the Empire also used S-thread boosters to blaze a secret [[Gandeal-Fondor Hyperlane|military hyperlane]] linking Fondor and the Core Worlds [[Fortress world/Legends|fortress world]] [[Gandeal]].<ref name="TEA" />

In addition, the Empire utilized non-mass S-thread boosters to maintain the [[Byss Run/Legends|Byss Run]] hyperlane in the Deep Core, which connected the Koros system&mdash;by then known as the Empress Teta system&mdash;and [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] personal retreat planet [[Byss/Legends|Byss]]. Imperial non-mass S-thread boosters were also used to extend the [[Silvestri Trace]] hyperlane from the planet [[Sullust/Legends|Sullust]]<ref name="TEA" /> of the Outer Rim's [[Brema sector/Legends|Brema sector]]<ref name="EAOC Sullust">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Sullust system/Legends|Sullust system]]</ref> to the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell sector]], with that [[Sector/Legends|sector's]] [[Murk system/Legends|Murk system]] becoming a penultimate stop on the new hyperspace route, known as the [[Sanctuary Pipeline/Legends|Sanctuary Pipeline]].<ref name="TEA" />

==Behind the scenes==
The S-thread booster was first introduced via mentions of the non-mass S-thread booster in the article "[[Endor and the Moddell Sector]]," which was authored by [[Craig Robert Carey]], [[Daniel Wallace]], and [[Jason Fry]] and was published in the [[Star Wars Gamer 9|ninth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Gamer]]'' magazine<ref name="Endor">{{GamerCite|9|Endor and the Moddell Sector}}</ref> on [[February 22]], [[2002]].<ref name="GamerDate">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/other/rpg/news20020222.html|text=Starfighters Soar in Gamer #9}}</ref> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' by Wallace and Fry subsequently identified the general technology as the S-thread booster.<ref name="TEA" />
